rationale: The base station reports active fault E-201 and shows 8/8 devices bound (max_devices=8), matching the app's device list with no orphaned bindings. The new door sensor fails to pair because the HB-100 capacity is full, not because the sensor is defective. Frontline can resolve by removing an unused device (e.g., the offline "Test Sensor") to free a slot.

repair_steps: In the app, go to Device Settings for the offline 'Test Sensor' and select Remove Device.
Confirm removal to free one device slot on the HB-100 base station.
Ask the customer to put the new door sensor into pairing mode and attempt pairing again.
If pairing succeeds, verify the new sensor appears in the app and shows online status.
output.customer_reply: I found the issue: your base station has reached its maximum of 8 connected devices, so the new sensor can't pair. I'll guide you to remove an unused device (the offline 'Test Sensor') to free a slot. After that, we'll pair your new door sensor. No need to return it.

results.text: The base station already holds its maximum number of bound peripherals. Frontline action: remove an unused device. Not an escalation case.

HB-100 supports up to 8 bound peripherals. HB-200 supports up to 16 bound peripherals. When the limit is reached, pairing a new device fails with error E-201 even if the device is in pairing mode. Remove an unused device in the app (Device Settings > Remove Device) to free a slot.

results.source: manual_base_station#Orphaned binding (device removed in app but still bound in base station)
results.text: If a device is removed in the app while it is offline or out of range, the base station may keep its entry. This orphaned ("ghost") binding still occupies a slot, so the base station can report E-201 although the app lists fewer devices than the limit. Frontline cannot clear it: the app only removes devices it lists, re-pairing does not free the slot, and a base-station factory reset is not allowed. Treat it as a binding-table inconsistency (app and base station disagree) and escalate to FAE, who remove the entry with the backend binding tool. Put the orphaned device id and the bound count (for example 8/8) in the ticket.

complaint: I bought a new door sensor last week but it just won't pair. I followed the instructions and held the button. The app shows an error with a code, and I have tried both my phone and my partner's phone with the same result. Our system has grown over the years and, honestly, I don't remember how many devices we have. Do I need to return the sensor?
